sources.source: Diagram named XPath 3.1 and XQuery 3.1 Type System Part 3: Atomic Types in § 2.7.4 Type System

datatype.name: xs:anyType
datatype.description: A generalisation that represents all datatypes.

datatype.name: xs:anySimpleType
datatype.description: A restriction of xs:anyType to just all atomic values and all finite-length lists of zero or more atomic values.

datatype.name: xs:anyAtomicType
datatype.description: A generalisation, representing any atomic item type.

datatype.name: xs:decimal
datatype.description: A real number that can be represented by decimal numerals.

datatype.name: xs:unsignedInt
datatype.description: Derived from by setting the value of maxInclusive to 4294967295.

datatype.name: xs:unsignedShort
datatype.description: Derived from by setting the value of maxInclusive to 65535.

datatype.name: xs:unsignedByte
datatype.description: Derived from by setting the value of maxInclusive to 255.

datatype.name: xs:duration
datatype.description: A duration of time without fixed endpoints.

datatype.name: xs:gDay
datatype.description: A whole Gregorian day within an arbitrary month and year.

datatype.name: xs:gMonth
datatype.description: A whole Gregorian month within an arbitrary year.

datatype.name: xs:gMonthDay
datatype.description: A whole day within a specific Gregorian month in an arbitrary year.

datatype.name: xs:gYearMonth
datatype.description: A whole Gregorian month in a specific Gregorian year.

datatype.name: xs:normalizedString
datatype.description: A string that doesn't contain the following characters: carriage return (#xD); line feed (#xA); line feed (#x9).

datatype.name: xs:token
datatype.description: An xs:normalizedString that has no leading or trailing spaces (#x20) and includes no internal sequences of two or more spaces.

datatype.name: xs:time
datatype.description: An instant in time that recurs at the same point in each calendar day, or that occurs in some arbitrary calendar day.

notes.p: See Types adopted from XML Schema
See Types adopted from XML Schema

datatype.name: xs:error
datatype.description: A union type. Also a generalized atomic type.

notes.p: Not expected to have any instances. See Types adopted from XML Schema

datatype.name: xs:numeric
datatype.description: A union type whose members are: , and .

notes.p: See Types adopted from XML Schema

datatype.name: sequence
datatype.description: One or more occurrences of an , or non-abstract sub-type of .

sources.source: Describes empty-sequence() as a special type.

datatype.name: item()
datatype.description: An item is either an atomic item, a GNode, or a function item.

sources.source: Matches all items, so not abstract?

notes.p: For more information, see Function items.
From XPath 4.0, function items have an identity property, which can be used to test whether two variables refer to the same function item or not.
A may be used to constrain the type of items that may be added to a map.

datatype.name: record()
datatype.description: May be used to constrain the type of items that may be added to a map.

datatype.name: gnode()
datatype.description: A generalized node. It is always either an or a .

datatype.name: jnode()
datatype.description: An encapsulation of a value as it appears within a tree of maps and arrays, typically (but not necessarily) obtained by parsing JSON texts.

notes.p: This alternative name is only used in documentation. It's not expected to be used in code.
While the concept of a node existed before 4.0, the term was introduced in 4.0 to differentiate between XML nodes and JSON nodes (see ).

datatype.name: document-node()
datatype.description: A wrapper node that represents an XML document.

datatype.name: enum()
datatype.description: A constraint on , restricting the set of valid values.
